_verification_note: Every focused command asserts a PROPERTY the slice's contract requires, never a pinned literal (no row/test counts, no migration number). Two intentional structural checks: (1) 'FROM chat_dm_safety_config WHERE singleton' appears EXACTLY twice in the migration — once in the recreated dm_safety_enabled() and once as assert_dm_allowed()'s single SELECT-INTO; the pre-fix assert_dm_allowed had three of its own plus dm_safety_enabled()'s = four reads, so a count of two proves the collapse. (2) the three PL/pgSQL locals the old body assigned in separate statements (v_sender_limit/v_target_limit/v_audit_enabled) are GONE — their values now come from the single record read. The runtime torn-read invariant itself is proven in chat-dm-safety-invariants.test.ts via pg_get_functiondef(assert_dm_allowed) asserting exactly one chat_dm_safety_config read and zero dm_safety_enabled() call inside the body (a true two-session interleave is not deterministically expressible because the read is a single statement by construction — the structural proof IS the proof). Reviewer must confirm the fail-closed regression rows actually assert deny behavior (missing-row, each capability flag, both block directions, sender+target rate) against the RECREATED functions, not merely that a describe block exists; that dm_safety_enabled()'s OWN observable semantics are pinned by a direct call (acceptance row 2b: missing singleton row -> false; each of the four toggles individually false -> false; all true -> true), proving the CREATE OR REPLACE preserved behaviour rather than only checking the downstream consumer; and that dm_current_read_allowed() (owned by 0031, out of scope) still behaves identically after dm_safety_enabled() is recreated.

security_review.reason: assert_dm_allowed() is the DD-55 fail-closed authority gate for cross-person DM abuse (block + rate-limit). This slice recreates its body AND recreates dm_safety_enabled() — the predicate a security-sensitive RLS policy on root (dd38-dd86-chat-schema-core's dm_current_read_allowed / chat_channels_dm / chat_members_dm / chat_messages_dm) depends on. A regression here is fail-OPEN on a safety gate: the security round must verify, against the migrated live DB, that after the refactor (1) a missing chat_dm_safety_config row still denies on ALL four flags (single-read record all-NULL → dm_safety_flags_enabled → false → safety_disabled; limits COALESCE to 0 → rate deny) — fail-closed is PRESERVED, not weakened; (2) each capability flag independently disabling the gate still holds; (3) chat_pair_blocked() is still checked in BOTH directions; (4) the raised exception text never varies by deny_reason; (5) the RAISE LOG line still fires only when audit_enabled and never leaks to any client (client_min_messages=warning clause intact); (6) dm_safety_enabled()'s recreated body preserves missing-row → false exactly (outer COALESCE over the singleton subquery, NOT the inner form which would return NULL on an empty row set); (7) app/app_worker/readonly still have zero grant/EXECUTE on the tables and functions; (8) the new pure helper dm_safety_flags_enabled leaks nothing (no table access, REVOKE PUBLIC). This is the exact class DD-102 waived once already; the fix closing it must not open a different hole.
